title: Approval of 251 Albert Street mixed-use development
subtitle: Also: Waterloo Street reconstruction tender, Wilfrid Laurier graduate house at 150-152 Albert Street, and a closed meeting.
overview: Council approved a zoning change for a seven-storey building at 251 Albert Street. It would hold 32 dwelling units, a spiritual centre and a child care centre for up to 25 children. The vote was {{vote:m4}}. Council also authorized a reduced-parking agreement under Section 40 of the Planning Act, with a minimum of 26 parking spaces. The financial security that staff proposed will be set at a lesser amount by the Commissioner in consultation with the applicant. The main concerns were pedestrian safety and child pick-up and drop-off on busy Albert Street.

Council awarded the tender for reconstruction of Waterloo Street and part of Moore Avenue South to Terracon Underground Ltd. for a total of $1,921,734.61 {{vote:m2}}. It also adopted an Official Plan Amendment and approved a zoning amendment so Wilfrid Laurier University can convert a heritage-designated semi-detached house at 150-152 Albert Street into a graduate house {{vote:m3}}.

Council met in closed session earlier in the afternoon on labour relations, emergency procedures training, tribunal updates and site selection. The minutes report no decisions from it. Residents can expect the Albert Street details to be worked out through site plan and the Section 40 agreement.

decisions.detail: Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-14 for a mixed-use building with housing, a spiritual use and a child care centre above the first storey {{vote:m4}}.
Council authorized a parking exemption requiring a minimum of 26 spaces, with the Commissioner directed to set a lesser financial security in consultation with the applicant.
Council adopted Official Plan Amendment No. 38, asked the Region to approve it, and approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-22-09 for 150-152 Albert Street {{vote:m3}}.
Council awarded RFT24-06 to Terracon Underground Ltd. for a total of $1,921,734.61 including unrecoverable HST {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Councillors said their main concern at 251 Albert Street was safety rather than parking, especially child pick-up and drop-off, drivers stopping with flashers on, and pedestrians on a busy street.

Staff said Section 40 lets the City tie parking relief to conditions such as reporting and transportation demand management. They described the financial security as a performance bond to make sure these measures are carried out.

The applicant's representatives said the child care centre was essential to the project. They accepted reporting and monitoring but said the proposed $750,000 security was too large to post up front and would not add parking.

Delegates said many visitors on Friday evenings and Saturdays do not drive, and that a nearby church had informally agreed to overflow parking. Many speakers described the centre as a safe community hub for students and families.

Staff said the loading-space exemption raised concerns about waste vehicles backing onto the road. They said loading would be reviewed in detailed design at site plan, and one councillor said a vehicle backing out of the site was a safety risk.
